extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners (USPTO practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance from the MPEP governing the content, form, correction, submission, and handling of drawings in U.S. patent applications (including consequences for noncompliance and required labeling/annotations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected drawings required and not held in abeyance
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required in reply to the Office action to avoid abandonment of the application. The requirement for corrected drawings will not be held in abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly in form paragraphs (e.g., 6.22, 6.22.01, 6.36). If changes are not accepted by the examiner applicant will be notified and informed of required corrective action in the next Office action. Failure to timely submit corrected drawings will result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement/New sheet labeling and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date of an application must be labeled in the top margin as either "Replacement Sheet" or "New Sheet" pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). Any replacement sheet of drawings shall include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended. The figure or figure number of an amended drawing should not be labeled as "amended." If a drawing figure is to be canceled, the appropriate figure must be removed from the replacement sheet and, where necessary, the remaining figures must be renumbered and appropriate changes made to the brief description of the several views of the drawings for consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional replacement sheets may be necessary to show renumbering. Replacement sheets must be labeled so as not to obstruct any portion of the drawing figures (see 37 CFR 1.84(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked-up/Annotated copy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A marked-up copy (annotated copy) of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, may be included and must be clearly labeled as "Annotated Sheet" and presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change(s). A marked-up copy must be provided when required by the examiner (37 CFR 1.121(d)(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 6.27 may be used to require a marked-up copy. The annotated sheet should be placed in the amendment or remarks section and labeled "Annotated Sheet." Failure to provide required annotated copies will result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must show every feature of the claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing in a nonprovisional application must show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. Conventional features whose detailed illustration is not essential may be illustrated in the form of a graphical drawing symbol or a labeled representation (e.g., a labeled rectangular box). Tables and sequence listings should not be duplicated in the drawings (37 CFR 1.83(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings do not comply, the examiner shall require additional illustration within not less than two months; corrections are subject to § 1.81(d). Use form paragraphs (e.g., 6.22.01, 6.36) to require illustration or cancellation of claim features that are not shown. No new matter should be entered in corrected drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration of improvements to old machines
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention consists of an improvement on an old machine the drawing must, when possible, exhibit in one or more views the improved portion itself disconnected from the old structure, and also in another view show so much only of the old structure as will suffice to show the connection of the invention therewith (37 CFR 1.83(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the drawings are incomplete under this requirement, corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required (see form paragraph 6.22.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for corrections and statutory periods (abandonment risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is given a shortened statutory period (generally TWO (2) MONTHS in certain Office actions) to submit new drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.81. Extensions of time may be obtained under 37 CFR 1.136(a) but cannot carry the date for reply beyond the statute's maximum period (e.g., six months under 35 U.S.C. 133). If corrected drawings are requested in a Notice of Allowability, they must be filed within three months of the mailing of the notice; extensions under 1.136 are not available for this three-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely submit replacement drawing sheets will result in abandonment. For drawings not of sufficient quality to permit examination a shortened TWO (2) MONTH period is used; for notice of allowability a THREE (3) MONTH non-extendable period is used (37 CFR 1.85(c), MPEP § 608.02(p)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality sufficient to permit examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be of sufficient quality to permit examination. If not, replacement drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required in reply to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the "do not permit examination" form paragraph should be rare and limited to instances where no examination can be performed due to poor drawing quality. Examiner Note suggests using PTOL-90 or PTO-90C as a cover sheet. If changes are not accepted, applicant will be informed of required corrective action in the next Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference character accuracy and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters must be properly applied: no single reference character used for two different parts or for a part and a modification of such part; different numbers must not refer to the same part; the drawings must include reference characters mentioned in the description and the drawings must not include reference characters not mentioned in the description (37 CFR 1.84(p)(4)-(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 6.22.02 (different numbers refer to same part), 6.22.03 (same number used for different parts), 6.22.06 (reference numbers mentioned in description not in drawings), and 6.22.07 (reference numbers in drawings not in specification) provide templates and examiner notes. Examiner may allow applicant to delete the reference characters from the description instead of adding them to the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's responsibility for completeness and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should ensure that the figures are correctly described in the brief description of the several views, that reference characters are properly applied, that no single reference character is used for two different parts or for a part and its modification, and that there are no superfluous illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One or more form paragraphs may be used to require correction. Examiner should ensure consistency with the specification and other sheets and may require replacement sheets or annotated sheets as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications in drawings: no mixed broken/solid-line depiction; illustrate described modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications may not be shown in broken lines on figures which show in solid lines another form of the invention. All modifications described must be illustrated, or the text canceled. This does not apply to mere reference to minor variations nor to well-known and conventional parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases: Ex parte Badger; Ex parte Peck. Use form paragraph 6.22.05 to require correction where Figure(s) show modified forms of construction in the same view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art figures handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures showing the prior art are usually unnecessary and should be canceled. However, where needed to understand applicant's invention, they may be retained if designated by a legend such as "Prior Art."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prior-art figure is not labeled, use form paragraph 6.36.01 to require designation and corrected drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of replacement drawings and new matter review
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets of replacement drawings will be routinely entered into the contents of the application. However, the examiner should review replacement sheets for new matter, necessity, and consistency with other sheets; if the examiner decides the sheets should not be entered, the examiner must provide complete, explicit reasoning and previously made entries will be marked "not entered."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 6.37 may be used to acknowledge receipt and indicate whether drawings are acceptable or unacceptable. If unacceptable because of new matter or noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d), the examiner must explain and may use PTOL-324 or PTOL-326 (Office Action Summary). Drawings will not be returned to applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO does not make drawing changes — applicant responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office does not make drawing changes. It is applicant's responsibility to ensure that the drawings are corrected. The Office will not release drawings for purposes of correction; new corrected drawings must be submitted when corrections are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 6.39 informs applicants the USPTO does not make drawing changes; 6.40 provides information on how to effect drawing changes (replacement sheets, explanation of changes in amendment/remarks). 6.41 is a reminder when applicant has previously been provided instructions. If an amendment states replacement sheets were filed but they are not in IFW, the examiner must notify applicant that replacement drawings were not received and not entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying indicia on drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia, if provided, should include the title of the invention, inventor's name, and application number, or docket number (if any) if an application number has not been assigned; this information must be placed on the front of each sheet and within the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include identifying indicia on each drawing sheet submitted after filing; ensures proper association with application and IFW/SCORE records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of canceled figures
rubrics_metrics.description: A canceled figure may be reinstated. An amendment should be made to the specification adding the brief description of the view if a canceled figure is reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow general amendment procedures and ensure consistency with other sheets and the specification to avoid new matter issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage formats and color restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white line drawings in provisional and nonprovisional utility applications and certain proceedings will be converted into TIFF images and stored in IFW. Design application line drawings and certain photographs/grayscale drawings will be stored in SCORE with a black and white copy in IFW. Color drawings and photographs are not permitted in international applications (PCT Rule 11.13). Except for international applications, color drawings/photos in utility and design applications will be stored in SCORE and a black and white copy in IFW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally submitted drawings on paper that are photographs or in color may be maintained in an artifact folder. See MPEP §§ 608.02(c) for specific storage rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for correction at allowance/issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If a corrected drawing is required or if an amended drawing does not comply at the time an application is allowed, the Office may notify the applicant in a notice of allowability and set a three-month period from the mail date of the notice of allowability within which the applicant must file a corrected drawing in compliance with § 1.84 or § 1.1026, as applicable, to avoid abandonment. This period is not extendable under § 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.85(c) and MPEP §§ 608.02(p), 608.02(w), and 1302.05. If corrections at allowance are necessary, supply corrected drawings within the three-month non-extendable period or risk abandonment.
